reasoning: Both sets are detailed, statistically careful plans, and each drops something the user explicitly asked for. Set B drops the PPO trading agents from Stage 4. Its spec lists 'Learned allocation agents' as out of scope ('a later stage'), and it also rules out cloud compute, which contradicts the user's occasional rented GPU. Set A drops the yahooquery cross-check and the user's list of 10 delisted names. It replaces them with FRED/EDGAR sources and a 30-change check set. Both sets wrongly route Sharadar through the nasdaq-data-link client instead of api.sharadar.com. B is slightly stronger on quant method: synthetic known-answer gates, calibration features, a one-shot holdout, and stated detectable effect sizes. A is also rigorous, with a hypothesis ledger, purged walk-forward, a lockbox and AD-23's backtest conventions, and it covers every stage component, PPO and GPU included. On build planning A is cleaner. One Phase-0 interface task freezes every boundary across data, server and app. Its data milestone carries 27 golden cases with exact oracles, and its spines can start on the interface's samples. B runs three interface tasks in parallel even though they import each other (the explorer interface has no dependency on the qserver schema it uses). B's M1 has no golden cases at all, its tasks titled 'spine' are labelled kind thicken / mode split, and its brief and AGENTS.md are stale and only describe S1. A has its own defects: CONSTRAINTS.md is missing although every packet points to it, the todo disagrees with the plan on some sizes and packages, and RF-03 is assigned to an S3 milestone. On balance, A's more complete stage coverage and sounder build graph outweigh B's somewhat stronger statistical method.
